thread_analysis.thread_summary: Secom Co. (contact Hirotaka Kotake) engages Allion (Itsuo Sakai, Masaya Iida) for Bluetooth SIG certification of a security sensor device, spanning September through November 2024. The thread covers the full lifecycle from quote/Invoice through registration finalization, Compliance Folder shipment, and post-registration derivative-model addition guidance, surfacing several small but genuinely distinct administrative/technical clarifications along the way.
all_questions_found: Is it still acceptable to finalize registration despite a yellow warning on the ICS Form within Submission Requirements, given that a Test Case Waiver (TCW) was already filed? (see thread_0035_case_01)

Why does the registration evidence document now look different/lower-quality than before, where should the existing registered product be selected when adding a derivative model, and does the SDoC from the download link match the Compliance Folder's SDoC? (see thread_0035_case_02)
Why wasn't a delivery slip included in the physically shipped Compliance Folder package? (see thread_0035_case_03)
Which name goes in which field (Username, signature Name, Listing Owner) of the registration/addition documents? (see thread_0035_case_04)

(Administrative, not separately cased) Standard quote/Invoice/payment timeline, registration confirmation document Q&A (SIG account login binding, derivative models requiring separate registration), Compliance Folder document checklist (operation manual draft-level acceptable, block diagram, outline drawing) with a noted option to reuse Japan radio-law type-certification submission documents if available, and the customer's internal delivery-slip/inspection-notice/invoice payment workflow -- all consistent with administrative content already documented in other threads.
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Case_01 introduces the Test Case Waiver (TCW) concept for the first time in this batch -- a formal mechanism that can resolve an apparent Review Page warning without blocking registration finalization. Case_02's documentation of the July 2024 Launch Studio-to-Qualification Workspace migration's effect on the registration evidence document's visual format/quality is a concrete, customer-facing detail that complements the already-documented structural/IOPT-scope changes from that same migration seen in other threads.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0035_case_01 through thread_0035_case_04 for case-specific decision logic.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See individual case files; case_01 carries the most consequential risk if misjudged in the opposite direction (i.e., a consultant overlooking a genuine unresolved warning by wrongly assuming a TCW covers it).
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: No significant consulting-side mistakes identified -- the consultant proactively flagged the Review Page warning and its TCW resolution before the customer could be alarmed by it, and provided thorough, multi-part answers to bundled customer questions.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a Review Page or similar pre-finalization screen shows a warning indicator, proactively explain its resolution status (e.g., an existing Test Case Waiver) rather than waiting for the customer to question it; and when a customer notices a registration document or evidence format has changed from what they've seen before, explain the underlying platform migration as the cause to prevent the customer from assuming something is wrong with their specific registration.
